title: The Gates of the Sri Yantra
hookLine: a wall around a home, with a gate in every side
carry: the goddess's home opens a gate on every side
tomorrow: one step through the gate, and the straight lines turn into what?

cards: A new deadbolt on the front door. And, the same afternoon, a grandmother who says a home's door should never feel shut to a guest. Both have a point.
The Sri Yantra's outer border manages to hold both. It's a wall, drawn as a square. But in the middle of each side the line breaks and steps outward into a gate.
A wall with a door facing every direction. It's a strange thing to draw around a home you mean to keep safe. Whoever drew it seems to have expected visitors from everywhere.

teach.b: That square is the bhupura, the earth enclosure: the outermost layer, the one closest to where anyone stands.

A verse of the Saundarya Lahari, a hymn to the Goddess that tradition credits to Adi Shankara, counts the parts of her dwelling, and three lines are among them, usually drawn as this border, one inside the next.
For those who worship with it, the bhupura is the threshold: worship begins here, at the gates, and moves inward, layer by layer, toward the Goddess at the center.
Some teachers add that the wall also guards, holding the sacred space in. Both readings sit together. And a grandmother's open door has a scripture too.

teach.h: ATITHI DEVO BHAVA: THE GUEST AS GOD.
teach.b: The Taittiriya Upanishad, sending students home from their teacher, tells them to treat mother, father and teacher as gods, and the guest as a god as well: atithi devo bhava. Hindu homes still say it.

teach.h: THE WEEK'S DOORS, ONE BY ONE.
teach.b: Now walk back through this week's doors. A packed bus, and one awareness in every seat. A wandering mind that can't leave, because God is everywhere.
Choose the good, and delight can be a door. The self like the space in a jar. Puja in the heart while the shrine is in a box.
And now its edge: a wall with a gate for every guest.

how: In Sri Vidya worship the yantra is approached from its outer square, the bhupura, and its gates, before the worshipper moves inward layer by layer.

s: the square border is the center of the Sri Yantra
it's the outermost layer, the bhupura: where the journey in begins.
the border's line breaks into a gate on each side
a wall with a door facing every direction.
the yantra's wall is there only to keep outsiders out

games.q: your friend's family is nervous about strangers at their big open house. what picture does the yantra's border offer?
o: a wall with gates: keep the space cared for, and keep every door able to open.
no wall at all: the yantra has only open gates and nothing to guard.
one gate only, facing the family's own side of the street.
games.why: the bhupura is a wall that breaks into a gate on every side, and a Hindu home says atithi devo bhava: the guest as god. caring for the space and welcoming the guest go together.

practice: Count, on your fingers, the doors that opened for you this week: a person who let you in, a friend who listened, a place that made room for you. Go slowly, one finger for each.
When you run out, rest your hands and let the count settle.
